text.p: Following are the main stories reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and cannot vouch for their accuracy.

- The government will use state funds to compensate spending increases of the energy sector after abolishing on January 1, 1997, the value added tax exemptions on fuel and some agricultural products. It will not increase energy tariffs. Food prices should not go up more than four percent at the beginning of next year, according to the Statistics department data.

- Newspaper journalists voted Rimas Okulicius the man of the year. The Panevezys resident resisted extortion attempts by an organised group of criminals on Christmas Eve, shooting four attackers in self-defence and injuring another four.
- The new education and science minister Zigmas Zinkevicius says both patriotism and morality are lacking in Lithuanian schools.
- Lithuanian GDP was 22,517 billion litas during 9 months of 1996 which is an 3.6 percent increase on the same period a year earlier.
- The public opinion is that the new parliament and government are active and decisive, Vytautas Landsbergis, the parliement chairman and leader of the Homeland Union party, says in an interview.
- The new head of the Customs department, Alvydas Budrys, will be appointed on January 2. He wants to crack down on smuggling.
